newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Oct c/a deficit soars to $2.41 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Oct c/a deficit soars to $2.41 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit soared to $2.41 billion in October from a $340.5 million shortfall a year earlier, preliminary figures from the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Friday.
NOTE - Figures are in millions of U.S. dollars.
The bank attributed the soaring deficit in October to a continued export slump amid a steady rise in imports, mainly of consumer goods.
Free-on-board exports rose only 1.5 percent year-on-year to $11.26 billion in October, while imports increased 16.9 percent to $12.98 billion.

Customs-cleared imports of food and consumer goods rose year-on-year 26.6 percent in October, compared with a 25.9 percent rise a year ago. Raw material imports grew by a moderate 7.7 percent, sharply lower than a 35.7 percent rise, the central bank said.
South Korea's trade deficit with its major trading partners widened in October both from a month earlier and from the same month in 1995.
Total trade deficits with the United States, Japan and the European Union stood at $3.77 billion in October, from $3.11 billion in September and a $2 billion shortfall in October 1995.
Letters of credit received in October fell 1.7 percent to $5.69 billion from a year earlier, while import licenses issued in the month rose 15.6 percent to $13.28 billion, the central bank said.
